answer: The glover buys kid skins by the dozen and enters every pair of gloves against the skin it was cut from. A sparrow pair bought from another town fails the ledger: at the shale of the skin the leather must match the glover's own cutting, and bought gloves fit wrong. Forging a pair means hiring a glover, buying false skins and paying 6,500, and the signal entry in the kid-skin ledger is read at every market, so gloves whose skin was never entered are taken from the stall.
